theory.intro: In similar figures every pair of corresponding sides is in the same ratio, so one known pair of corresponding sides unlocks all the rest. Use the pair whose lengths are **both given** to calculate the scale factor, then multiply or divide by it to find the unknown side.
facts: $k=\frac{\text{image length}}{\text{original length}}$, calculated from the pair of corresponding sides with both lengths given.
To find a side of the **image**, multiply the corresponding original side by $k$; to find a side of the **original**, divide the corresponding image side by $k$.
If the image is smaller than the original, $k<1$ — multiplying by it correctly makes the image sides shorter.
The same working can be set out as equal fractions of corresponding sides, e.g. $\frac{x}{6}=\frac{14}{4}$ — keep the unknown in the numerator.
steps: Identify the pair of corresponding sides with both lengths given.
Calculate the scale factor: divide the image length by the original length.
Multiply an original side by the scale factor, or divide an image side by it, to find the unknown side.

mastery.question_text: Two similar triangles have corresponding sides of $8$ cm (original) and $20$ cm (image). The perimeter of the original triangle is $26$ cm. Find the perimeter of the image.
mastery.solution_text:
$k=\frac{\text{image}}{\text{original}}=\frac{20}{8}=2.5$
Every side is multiplied by $2.5$, so the perimeter is too.
$P=26\times2.5$
$=65\text{ cm}$

Ben matched the image's $10$ cm side with the original's $15$ cm side, but the $10$ cm side is the image's short side, so it corresponds to the original's $6$ cm side.
$k=\frac{10}{6}=\frac{5}{3}$
$x=15\times\frac{5}{3}$
$=25\text{ cm}$
